watercolor_simulation_hint: Water carries pigment across paper; as the brush unloads and water evaporates, clustered pigment creates granulation and darker drying edges. Try a wash, then a dry brush.

separation_tip_desc: When pigments with different mobility meet on wet paper, higher settings let faster color channels travel ahead of heavier ones. Premixed pigments remain more uniform.
rewetting_tip_desc: Clear water and wet glazes reactivate low-staining color more readily. Highly staining and strongly granulating layers stay anchored in the paper.
paper_chemistry_tip_desc: Higher sizing keeps water and pigment near the surface, extending flow and making dry color easier to lift. Lower sizing pulls washes into the fibers sooner. Bloom sensitivity controls how strongly wetness boundaries create backruns and cauliflower edges.
watercolor_science_desc: Water diffuses pigment into nearby paper fibers. Every deposited wash carries its own granulation, staining, opacity, and mobility through mixtures. Each color channel retains mobility-weighted transport, so faster pigments can separate at wet edges while heavier colors lag and settle. Granulating particles collect in texture, staining colors resist lifting, and opaque particles scatter more light. Paper sizing controls how long water and pigment remain mobile on the surface before absorption; highly sized sheets lift and rewet more readily, while lightly sized sheets anchor washes sooner. Bloom sensitivity controls the strength of backruns at uneven wetness boundaries. Dry layers can be selectively remobilized by clear water or wet glazes; low-staining color releases more readily while staining and granulation anchor pigment in the fibers. Studio humidity slows evaporation and preserves blooms, while airflow accelerates surface drying. Round, flat, mop, rigger, wash, and dry brushes vary footprint, softness, water load, spacing, and reservoir drain. Slow, pressured strokes deposit more paint, stylus tilt spreads the footprint, and optical absorption deepens mixtures. Masking fluid, evaporation, gravity, clear water, salt, blooms, and tide marks remain physically layered. Wetness maps and flow guides visualize the simulation without changing saved artwork.

sculpt_draw_lathe_help: Click on the pad to add a point, drag a point to move it. Points run from the bottom to the top; the dashed line is the spin axis.
sculpt_draw_extrude_help: Click on the pad to add a point after the nearest one, drag a point to move it. The outline closes itself.
fractal_keyboard_instructions: Keyboard: use the Zoom, Horizontal pan, and Vertical pan sliders to explore every view. Pointer users can also double-click a location or use the mouse wheel.
julia_parameter_connection_explained: use the same formula but fix c and vary the starting z. For z squared plus c, parameters in the Mandelbrot set give connected Julia sets; parameters outside it give disconnected, dust-like Cantor Julia sets. The Fatou set is the complement of the Julia set.
gradient_interpolation_explained: follows a path around the hue circle. RGB interpolation blends channel values: halfway between pure red and pure blue is purple, not gray. Neither HSL nor RGB is perceptually uniform; spaces such as OKLab are designed for more even perceived changes. A hue path and a pigment mixture describe different processes.
learning_artist_el_anatsui_overview: Transforms discarded bottle caps and metal into vast, flexible fields that change with every installation.
learning_artist_el_anatsui_lookFor: Repetition, material history, changing surfaces, and the tension between precious appearance and discarded matter.
learning_artist_el_anatsui_context: His works connect trade, consumption, colonial histories, labor, and the ability of a material to carry memory.
learning_artist_el_anatsui_tryThis: Build a repeated unit from safe reused material, then test three arrangements instead of treating the first layout as final.
learning_artist_el_anatsui_respect: Study transformation and systems; do not reduce West African histories to a decorative metallic effect.
learning_artist_ibrahim_el_salahi_overvi: A foundational figure in African modernism whose drawings and paintings join calligraphic energy, memory, landscape, and abstraction.
learning_artist_ibrahim_el_salahi_lookFo: Branching lines, compressed figures, black-and-white rhythm, and forms that hover between writing and image.
learning_artist_ibrahim_el_salahi_contex: His work emerged through Sudanese, African, Arab, Islamic, and international modernist conversations rather than a single inherited category.
learning_artist_ibrahim_el_salahi_tryThi: Let one continuous line grow into an image, then identify where it reads as symbol, body, landscape, or writing.
learning_artist_ibrahim_el_salahi_respec: Explore the relationship between mark and meaning without copying sacred or unfamiliar scripts as decoration.
learning_artist_esther_mahlangu_overview: Extends Ndebele mural painting through architecture, canvas, vehicles, and public commissions while asserting the knowledge of women artists.
learning_artist_esther_mahlangu_lookFor: Bold boundaries, geometric sequencing, high-contrast color, scale, and the adaptation of a living mural practice.
learning_artist_esther_mahlangu_context: Ndebele house painting is a living cultural practice tied to community, identity, and women’s knowledge—not a generic pattern library.
learning_artist_esther_mahlangu_tryThis: Create a geometric rhythm from shapes drawn from your own environment and explain what your repeated choices mean.
learning_artist_esther_mahlangu_respect: Credit Ndebele artists and context. Do not claim Ndebele identity or reproduce culturally meaningful motifs as anonymous décor.
learning_artist_skunder_boghossian_place: Ethiopia, France, and the United States
learning_artist_skunder_boghossian_overv: Built dense, layered paintings from Ethiopian visual histories, personal symbols, jazz-like rhythm, and international modernism.
learning_artist_skunder_boghossian_lookF: Layering, icon-like forms, luminous color, improvisation, and figures emerging from complex grounds.
learning_artist_skunder_boghossian_conte: His work challenges accounts of modernism that place innovation only in Europe and North America.
learning_artist_skunder_boghossian_tryTh: Layer three translucent systems—marks, shapes, and a limited palette—then decide which layer should lead.
learning_artist_skunder_boghossian_respe: Study how multiple histories coexist in a work rather than extracting Ethiopian symbols from their meanings.
learning_artist_hokusai_overview: Used woodblock design, dramatic cropping, repeated series, and close observation to make everyday labor and landscape feel monumental.
learning_artist_hokusai_lookFor: Strong silhouettes, compressed depth, directional movement, foreground cropping, and recurring viewpoints.
learning_artist_hokusai_context: Ukiyo-e prints were collaborative works involving designer, carver, printer, and publisher—not the product of one isolated hand.
learning_artist_hokusai_tryThis: Compose the same place from three viewpoints using only flat shapes and a four-color palette.
learning_artist_hokusai_respect: Name the collaborative print process and avoid treating Japanese design as a timeless exotic aesthetic.
learning_artist_amrita_sher_gil_overview: Joined European painting study with sustained attention to people, color, and social life in India, refusing an easy division between East and West.
learning_artist_amrita_sher_gil_lookFor: Weighted figures, quiet group psychology, earthy color, simplified volume, and carefully held space.
learning_artist_amrita_sher_gil_context: Her work belongs to histories of Indian modernism, migration, gender, and the unequal conditions through which art histories are written.
learning_artist_amrita_sher_gil_tryThis: Arrange three simplified figures so posture and spacing communicate a relationship without facial detail.
learning_artist_amrita_sher_gil_respect: Study composition and social attention rather than using clothing or identity as costume.
learning_artist_pacita_abad_places: The Philippines and a global studio practice
learning_artist_pacita_abad_overview: Created exuberant trapunto paintings by stitching, stuffing, painting, and attaching materials to build color into physical relief.
learning_artist_pacita_abad_lookFor: Quilted depth, accumulated surfaces, portable materials, intense color, and the movement between abstraction and social witness.
learning_artist_pacita_abad_context: Her global practice grew through travel and relationships; it should not be flattened into a collection of interchangeable cultural motifs.
learning_artist_pacita_abad_tryThis: Design a relief surface in three layers: base shape, stitched or repeated boundary, and attached texture.
learning_artist_pacita_abad_respect: Credit specific material traditions when using them and avoid presenting cultural borrowing as placeless “world pattern.”
learning_artist_yayoi_kusama_overview: Uses repetition, mirrored space, accumulation, performance, painting, and sculpture to alter how a viewer experiences body and environment.
learning_artist_yayoi_kusama_lookFor: Accumulation, serial marks, scale shifts, reflection, immersion, and the point where repetition changes perception.
learning_artist_yayoi_kusama_context: Her long practice cannot be reduced to polka dots; it includes painting, political performance, publishing, fashion, sculpture, and installation.
learning_artist_yayoi_kusama_tryThis: Choose one simple mark and vary density and scale until the surrounding space—not the mark itself—becomes the subject.
learning_artist_yayoi_kusama_respect: Study repetition and perception in Kusama’s work; develop your own visual decisions instead of copying a signature composition.
learning_artist_artemisia_gentileschi_ov: Built large narrative paintings through forceful gesture, directional light, compressed action, and protagonists with physical presence.
learning_artist_artemisia_gentileschi_lo: Chiaroscuro, diagonals, weight, hands at work, and the moment in a story selected for maximum consequence.
learning_artist_artemisia_gentileschi_co: Her biography matters, but reducing every painting to personal trauma can erase her professional ambition, learning, patrons, and invention.
learning_artist_artemisia_gentileschi_tr: Stage a three-shape scene where light and diagonal movement identify the decisive moment without adding text.
learning_artist_artemisia_gentileschi_re: Do not treat an artist’s suffering as the only explanation for artistic intelligence.
learning_artist_kathe_kollwitz_overview: Used drawing, etching, lithography, woodcut, and sculpture to address grief, labor, poverty, war, care, and resistance.
learning_artist_kathe_kollwitz_lookFor: Compressed value, expressive hands, repeated figures, carved silhouettes, and empathy without sentimentality.
learning_artist_kathe_kollwitz_context: Printmaking allowed images to circulate beyond a single painting, joining formal decisions to public witness.
learning_artist_kathe_kollwitz_tryThis: Tell a social story using only black, paper color, and three values; remove every mark that does not carry meaning.
learning_artist_kathe_kollwitz_respect: Approach represented suffering with specificity and dignity, not as visual drama detached from people’s lives.
learning_artist_hilma_af_klint_overview: Developed large abstract systems of color, geometry, notation, and organic form years before abstraction entered the standard modernist story.
learning_artist_hilma_af_klint_lookFor: Paired forms, spirals, diagrams, botanical growth, letter-like signs, scale, and sequences across groups of works.
learning_artist_hilma_af_klint_context: Her practice joined artistic experiment, spiritual inquiry, scientific curiosity, collaboration, and careful systems of documentation.
learning_artist_hilma_af_klint_tryThis: Invent five nonverbal forms for growth, tension, balance, change, and return; arrange them as a visual argument.
learning_artist_hilma_af_klint_respect: Distinguish studying symbolic systems from claiming that unfamiliar spiritual signs have meanings you invented.
learning_artist_bridget_riley_overview: Builds precise arrangements of line, interval, contrast, and color that make perception feel unstable and active.
learning_artist_bridget_riley_lookFor: Rhythm, optical vibration, repeated intervals, figure-ground reversal, and movement produced without animation.
learning_artist_bridget_riley_context: Op art is not merely an illusion trick; it asks how seeing unfolds over time in an embodied viewer.
learning_artist_bridget_riley_tryThis: Change one interval across a repeated grid and record where still pattern begins to appear mobile.
learning_artist_bridget_riley_respect: Riley is a living artist. Investigate perceptual variables rather than copying a recognizable composition.
learning_artist_tarsila_do_amaral_overvi: Combined vivid color, transformed bodies and landscapes, industrial change, and Brazilian modernist debates into an unmistakable visual language.
learning_artist_tarsila_do_amaral_lookFo: Elastic scale, simplified volume, saturated local color, landscape-body relationships, and tension between city and countryside.
learning_artist_tarsila_do_amaral_contex: Brazilian modernism wrestled with colonial inheritance and national identity; cultural cannibalism was a critical strategy, not a decorative theme.
learning_artist_tarsila_do_amaral_tryThi: Exaggerate the scale of one ordinary form to show how power or attention operates in a place you know.
learning_artist_tarsila_do_amaral_respec: Study transformation and national self-definition without turning Brazilian identity into tropical shorthand.
learning_artist_wifredo_lam_overview: Created hybrid, compressed figures amid cane-like vegetation while confronting colonialism and the European appetite for primitivism.
learning_artist_wifredo_lam_lookFor: Mask-like heads, blade forms, unstable bodies, dense vertical space, and figures that resist easy reading.
learning_artist_wifredo_lam_context: Lam engaged Afro-Cuban histories and modernism while rejecting the treatment of African and Caribbean culture as raw material for Europe.
learning_artist_wifredo_lam_tryThis: Construct a figure from plant, tool, and body shapes so no single category fully explains it.
learning_artist_wifredo_lam_respect: Do not call unfamiliar sacred or cultural forms “primitive,” and do not detach Afro-Cuban references from colonial history.
learning_artist_frida_kahlo_overview: Made tightly constructed paintings in which body, disability, clothing, plants, politics, place, and self-representation carry layered meanings.
learning_artist_frida_kahlo_lookFor: Direct gaze, compressed symbols, doubled selves, bodily specificity, staged space, and objects functioning as evidence.
learning_artist_frida_kahlo_context: Her work exceeds the simplified label “pain transformed into art”; it also involves humor, politics, national identity, intimacy, and deliberate self-fashioning.
learning_artist_frida_kahlo_tryThis: Create a symbolic self-portrait without drawing a face: choose five objects and explain what relationship each one carries.
learning_artist_frida_kahlo_respect: Do not romanticize disability or reduce a complex artist to trauma and inspirational perseverance.
learning_artist_joaquin_torres_garcia_ov: Organized grids, pictographic signs, proportion, and a School of the South that reoriented modern art away from Europe as the automatic center.
learning_artist_joaquin_torres_garcia_lo: Modular grids, unequal rectangles, compact signs, primary colors, and relationships between universal systems and local place.
learning_artist_joaquin_torres_garcia_co: His inverted map of South America made orientation itself an argument: north need not determine cultural authority.
learning_artist_joaquin_torres_garcia_tr: Design a grid-map of your community using only ten personal symbols, then rotate it and ask what the new orientation changes.
learning_artist_joaquin_torres_garcia_re: Invent symbols from your own life instead of borrowing Indigenous signs as supposedly universal marks.
learning_artist_etel_adnan_places: Lebanon, France, and the United States
learning_artist_etel_adnan_overview: Moved among poetry, painting, tapestry, leporello books, journalism, and philosophy, often returning to compact landscapes and the changing presence of a mountain.
learning_artist_etel_adnan_lookFor: Small fields of strong color, horizon, sun, folded sequence, repeated place, and the exchange between writing and image.
learning_artist_etel_adnan_context: Her multilingual, diasporic practice resists being assigned to one nation, language, medium, or identity.
learning_artist_etel_adnan_tryThis: Observe the same view at three times and reduce each version to five color shapes; bind them into a sequence.
learning_artist_etel_adnan_respect: Treat migration and multilingual identity as lived complexity, not as an exotic source of visual hybridity.
learning_artist_shirin_neshat_overview: Uses photography, film, sound, performance, and divided installations to examine power, gender, exile, collective voice, and representation.
learning_artist_shirin_neshat_lookFor: Black-white contrast, opposing screens, gaze, calligraphic overlay, sound across space, and individuals positioned within groups.
learning_artist_shirin_neshat_context: Her work addresses Iranian and diasporic histories while also questioning Western expectations about Muslim women.
learning_artist_shirin_neshat_tryThis: Storyboard two simultaneous viewpoints on the same event and decide what each frame allows or withholds.
learning_artist_shirin_neshat_respect: Neshat is a living artist. Do not imitate her signature imagery or use pseudo-calligraphy; study viewpoint, opposition, and spectatorship.
learning_artist_monir_farmanfarmaian_ove: Joined mirror mosaic, reverse-glass painting, geometry, craft collaboration, and modern abstraction in radiant constructed works.
learning_artist_monir_farmanfarmaian_loo: Reflection, polygon systems, cut modules, changing light, symmetry, and the viewer becoming part of the surface.
learning_artist_monir_farmanfarmaian_con: Her work grew through Iranian architectural and craft traditions as well as international abstraction; neither side is a decorative footnote.
learning_artist_monir_farmanfarmaian_try: Build a symmetric polygon system whose appearance changes when a light source or viewer position moves.
learning_artist_monir_farmanfarmaian_res: Credit mirror-work traditions and workshop collaboration rather than describing the work as geometry discovered by modernism alone.
learning_artist_laila_shawa_overview: Combined screenprint, photography, painting, text, pattern, and pop color to confront occupation, gender, violence, propaganda, and mass media.
learning_artist_laila_shawa_lookFor: Repetition, photographic fragments, bright color against difficult content, fences or grids, and images transformed through printing.
learning_artist_laila_shawa_context: Surface attraction and political critique operate together; brightness does not make the subject uncomplicated.
learning_artist_laila_shawa_tryThis: Repeat one news-derived shape, changing scale and color to reveal how repetition can normalize or challenge a message.
learning_artist_laila_shawa_respect: Keep political images connected to real histories and people; do not aestheticize violence into an empty pattern.
learning_artist_alma_thomas_overview: Developed luminous abstractions from gardens, music, light, and space exploration after a long career as a public-school art teacher.
learning_artist_alma_thomas_lookFor: Broken color marks, white intervals, vertical and circular rhythm, optical mixing, and movement built from small variation.
learning_artist_alma_thomas_context: Thomas became Howard University’s first fine-arts graduate and produced her best-known work after retiring from thirty-five years of teaching.
learning_artist_alma_thomas_tryThis: Build a rhythm from separated color marks, leaving the ground active; vary one interval so the pattern breathes rather than becoming mechanical.
learning_artist_alma_thomas_respect: Study rhythm, nature, and late-life experimentation rather than copying a signature mosaic surface.
learning_artist_ruth_asawa_overview: Created suspended looped-wire forms whose interior and exterior remain visible, while also building arts education and public-making programs.
learning_artist_ruth_asawa_lookFor: Continuous line in space, nested volume, transparency, shadow, hand process, and structures that hold air rather than conceal it.
learning_artist_ruth_asawa_context: Her work connects craft knowledge, experimental education, unjust wartime incarceration, family, public art, and sustained community organizing.
learning_artist_ruth_asawa_tryThis: Model a volume using only a continuous line or mesh; make its shadow a second composition.
learning_artist_ruth_asawa_respect: Do not use incarceration as an inspirational prelude; recognize it as state violence within a larger life and practice.
learning_artist_jacob_lawrence_overview: Built narrative series from repeated colors, angular figures, research, text, and scenes of migration, labor, resistance, and everyday life.
learning_artist_jacob_lawrence_lookFor: Series structure, recurring palette, diagonals, compressed rooms, repeated figures, and the relation between caption and image.
learning_artist_jacob_lawrence_context: The Migration Series treats history through many connected panels, making movement and collective experience structural rather than incidental.
learning_artist_jacob_lawrence_tryThis: Tell one community change in four panels using a fixed six-color palette and one recurring shape.
learning_artist_jacob_lawrence_respect: Research the people and history represented; do not turn collective struggle into a generic heroic storyline.
learning_artist_maria_martinez_overview: Worked with family and community collaborators to refine celebrated black-on-black pottery grounded in Pueblo knowledge and material practice.
learning_artist_maria_martinez_lookFor: Form, burnished and matte contrast, firing knowledge, surface-light relationships, and the precision of a vessel as a whole.
learning_artist_maria_martinez_context: Maria Martinez’s pottery is inseparable from San Ildefonso Pueblo, family collaboration, clay knowledge, firing, and the pressures of an outside art market.
learning_artist_maria_martinez_tryThis: Design a vessel through silhouette and two surface finishes; explain how light—not borrowed motif—creates contrast.
learning_artist_maria_martinez_respect: Pueblo designs are not a pattern pack. Credit Maria, Julian Martinez, family collaborators, San Ildefonso Pueblo, and living pottery traditions.
learning_artist_emily_kame_kngwarreye_ov: Began painting on canvas late in life after decades of cultural and artistic work, creating varied paintings grounded in Alhalker Country and Anmatyerr knowledge.
learning_artist_emily_kame_kngwarreye_lo: Gesture, seasonal change, layered mark, scale, Country, and dramatic shifts between dense fields and spare lines.
learning_artist_emily_kame_kngwarreye_co: The work is not generic abstraction: it arises from Country, kinship, plants, ceremony, and knowledge that viewers do not automatically possess.
learning_artist_emily_kame_kngwarreye_tr: Map change in a place you personally know through gesture, density, and season rather than copying dots or cultural symbols.
learning_artist_emily_kame_kngwarreye_re: Do not copy Anmatyerr marks or claim their meanings. Learn from sustained attention to your own relationship with place.
learning_artist_lisa_reihana_overview: Uses photography, moving image, sound, performance, costume, and digital compositing to question colonial representation and reactivate histories.
learning_artist_lisa_reihana_lookFor: Panoramic sequence, staged encounter, gaze, costume, sound, quotation, and the difference between being pictured and representing oneself.
learning_artist_lisa_reihana_context: Her work often speaks back to European images of the Pacific rather than simply illustrating the historical record they created.
learning_artist_lisa_reihana_tryThis: Take one historical image and storyboard what occurs immediately outside its frame from another participant’s viewpoint.
learning_artist_lisa_reihana_respect: Reihana is a living Māori artist. Study counter-narrative and framing; do not imitate culturally specific imagery or performance.
learning_artist_yuki_kihara_overview: Works across photography, performance, video, dance, and curating to examine colonial imagery, climate, gender, labor, and Sāmoan histories.
learning_artist_yuki_kihara_lookFor: Re-enactment, serial photographs, pose, archival quotation, costume, absence, and who controls the camera.
learning_artist_yuki_kihara_context: Kihara’s perspective as a faʻafafine artist is specific; it should not be translated into a generic Western category or spectacle.
learning_artist_yuki_kihara_tryThis: Restage the composition—not the identity or costume—of an archival image and change who has agency in the frame.
learning_artist_yuki_kihara_respect: Kihara is a living artist. Use the work to study power in representation, not to imitate Sāmoan or faʻafafine identity.
learning_artist_fiona_foley_overview: Uses sculpture, photography, public art, text, and research to expose colonial violence, contested language, memory, and Badtjala histories.
learning_artist_fiona_foley_lookFor: Encoded text, archival evidence, public placement, material symbolism, withheld information, and work that changes as history is uncovered.
learning_artist_fiona_foley_context: Her projects demonstrate that public monuments and official archives are active political forms, not neutral containers of facts.
learning_artist_fiona_foley_tryThis: Identify a phrase or omission in a local public record and design a nonliteral memorial that asks viewers to investigate it.
learning_artist_fiona_foley_respect: Foley is a living Badtjala artist. Research local Indigenous authority and history rather than borrowing her symbols or speaking for her community.
learning_artist_comparison_prompt_0: What appears similar at first, and what different histories or purposes change its meaning?
learning_artist_comparison_prompt_1: How does each material or process shape what the artist can ask a viewer to notice?
learning_artist_comparison_prompt_2: Which underlying decision could you translate into your own context without copying identity, symbols, or a signature style?
learning_use_one_prompt_or_ignore_the_gu: Use one prompt, or ignore the guide and follow what the work needs.
learning_explore_one_variable_at_a_time_: Explore one variable at a time, save a study, and compare what changed.
learning_what_do_you_want_to_make_b89d37: What do you want to make?
learning_choose_a_creative_direction_the: Choose a creative direction. The canvas comes first; techniques, artists, mathematics, and accessibility stay close when you want to look deeper.
learning_review_your_last_art_studio_pro: Review your last Art Studio project on the Process Shelf
learning_compare_the_decisions_you_kept_: Compare the decisions you kept, changed, and questioned.
learning_follow_one_idea_through_three_l: Follow one idea through three labs
learning_a_creative_thread_gives_you_a_f: A Creative Thread gives you a flexible brief and keeps your next step nearby. Explore freely; your place will wait.
learning_replace_saved_study_for_this_th: Replace saved study for this thread step

learning_save_this_static_image_as_a_vis: Save this static image as a Visual Support
learning_artwork_handoff_is_available_in: Artwork handoff is available in canvas labs.
learning_a_wider_map_of_artistic_intelli: A wider map of artistic intelligence
learning_explore_artists_across_seven_re: Explore artists across seven regions, many media, and different relationships among art, place, history, technology, and community. No profile is a style preset: notice decisions, investigate context, and make from your own experience.
learning_choose_at_least_one_more_profil: Choose at least one more profile to begin a side-by-side inquiry.
learning_compare_context_and_choices_wit: Compare context and choices without flattening distinct practices into a shared style.
learning_clear_one_or_more_filters_to_re: Clear one or more filters to return to the full explorer.
learning_carry_the_inquiry_into_a_studio: Carry the inquiry into a Studio lab
learning_searches_sourcebook_providers_a: Searches Sourcebook providers and fails closed: no result appears unless its item-level rights pass the selected allowlist.
learning_rights_filter_for_artist_collec: Rights filter for artist collection search
learning_sourcebook_s_verified_provider_: Sourcebook’s verified provider service will load on demand. If it cannot load, Art Studio shows no substitute results.
learning_external_collection_records_are: External collection records are for further study. Rights vary by individual artwork; this tab does not grant reuse permission or reproduce those works.
learning_nothing_was_shown_because_no_co: Nothing was shown because no collection result passed both relevance and the active rights allowlist.

process_restore_toast: Study restored to the Process Shelf.

process_archive_help: Archived work stays intact until you choose to restore it.

process_scope_label: Choose which Art Studio studies to show
process_no_view_studies: No studies are in this view yet.
process_first_study: Your first study will become a checkpoint.
process_archive_empty_help: Archive an active study when you want to clear space without losing it.

process_comparison_prompt: What stayed consistent? What became clearer? Which decision better serves your intention?
guide_simple_artistExplorer_try: Choose one artist. Find a color, shape, or material they use.
guide_simple_artistExplorer_notice: How does that choice help tell a story?
guide_simple_artistExplorer_stretch: Use a related idea to make something of your own.
guide_simple_artistExplorer_definition: A decision about color, shape, material, or meaning.
guide_simple_colorWheel_try: Pick a color. Make a bright version and a dull version.
guide_simple_colorWheel_notice: What changes when you move lightness?
guide_simple_colorWheel_stretch: Choose one color to stand out.
guide_simple_colorWheel_definition: The color family, such as red, green, or blue.
guide_simple_mixer_try: Choose two colors. Try mixing them as paint and as light.
guide_simple_mixer_notice: Do both mixtures look the same?
guide_simple_mixer_stretch: Guess the next mixture before changing the amounts.
guide_simple_mixer_definition: The material that gives paint its color.
guide_simple_watercolor_try: Use one paint color. Try one wet mark and one dry mark.
guide_simple_watercolor_notice: Watch the edges as the paint moves.
guide_simple_watercolor_stretch: Make three marks with different amounts of water.
guide_simple_watercolor_definition: A layer of paint spread with water.
guide_simple_pixel_try: Start with a small grid. Draw the outside shape first.
guide_simple_pixel_notice: Which squares make the shape easy to recognize?
guide_simple_pixel_stretch: Use only four colors. Look at the small preview.
guide_simple_pixel_definition: The outside shape of an object, without its inside details.
guide_simple_symmetry_try: Draw one mark away from the center.
guide_simple_symmetry_notice: Watch how the tool repeats your mark.
guide_simple_symmetry_stretch: Try another symmetry mode. Compare the patterns.
guide_simple_symmetry_definition: A match between parts of a shape after a flip or turn.
guide_simple_spirograph_try: Change one circle size. Keep the other settings the same.
guide_simple_spirograph_notice: How does the loop pattern change?
guide_simple_spirograph_stretch: Find two settings that make similar shapes.
guide_simple_spirograph_definition: A way to compare two amounts, such as two circle sizes.
guide_simple_generative_notice: Look at where the particles gather.
guide_simple_generative_stretch: Keep the seed. Change one setting and compare at the same step.
guide_simple_generative_definition: A starting number that lets the tool repeat its random choices.
guide_simple_spinArt_try: Put paint near the center, then near the edge.
guide_simple_spinArt_notice: How does the paint spread in each place?
guide_simple_spinArt_stretch: Use the same colors to make a calm area and a busy area.
guide_simple_stringArt_try: Connect every third point. Then try every fifth point.
guide_simple_stringArt_notice: Where do the straight lines seem to make a curve?
guide_simple_stringArt_definition: A line that bends instead of staying straight.
guide_simple_opArt_try: Repeat a pattern. Change the spaces between its parts.
guide_simple_opArt_notice: Does any part look as if it is moving?
guide_simple_opArt_stretch: Try softer color differences. Compare what you notice.
guide_simple_opArt_definition: A visible difference between nearby colors or shapes.
guide_simple_tessellation_try: Repeat one tile to fill the space.
guide_simple_tessellation_notice: Look for the shapes between the tiles.
guide_simple_tessellation_stretch: Repeat colors in a new order.
guide_simple_tessellation_definition: One shape used again and again to make a pattern.
guide_simple_fractal_try: Make a small change to one setting. Zoom toward an edge.
guide_simple_fractal_notice: What details appear as you zoom?
guide_simple_fractal_stretch: Save two views. Find a shape they have in common.
guide_simple_fractal_definition: How large or small something is shown.
guide_simple_gradient_try: Choose three color stops. Move the middle one.
guide_simple_gradient_notice: Which color takes up more space now?
guide_simple_gradient_stretch: Make one part of the blend stand out.
guide_simple_gradient_definition: A chosen color at one position in a blend.
guide_simple_stereogram_try: Choose a simple depth shape and a repeating pattern.
guide_simple_stereogram_notice: Look for the hidden shape, or explore the depth map.
guide_simple_stereogram_stretch: Try a smaller depth difference. Compare both versions.
guide_simple_stereogram_definition: How near or far a part of a picture seems to be.
guide_simple_sculpt3d_try: Put three shapes together. Turn the view.
guide_simple_sculpt3d_notice: How does the outside shape change as you turn?
guide_simple_sculpt3d_stretch: Choose a different view. Adjust one shape.
guide_simple_sculpt3d_definition: The position from which you look at something.
guide_simple_contrast_try: Choose a text color and a background color.
guide_simple_contrast_notice: Check the result. Change just the text color.
guide_simple_contrast_stretch: Keep a pair that meets the target and suits your artwork.
guide_simple_contrast_definition: A number comparing how light or dark two colors are.
guide_simple_harmonyHunt_try: Compare two sound or color combinations.
guide_simple_harmonyHunt_notice: Which parts seem to fit together?
guide_simple_harmonyHunt_stretch: Use one combination to inspire a visual pattern.
guide_simple_harmonyHunt_definition: How many times something repeats in one second.
compare_seed_unknown: The seed or step was not saved for one of these studies. Save new studies to make a controlled comparison.
artist_search_help: Accents are optional. Each search word can match anywhere in a profile.
artist_selected_announcement: Selected {name} in Artists and Traditions Explorer
process_search_help: Find titles, notes, intentions, or labs in this view.
process_compare_choose_second: Choose one more study to compare.
process_search_empty_help: Try another word, clear the search, or choose another view.
